newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan takes delivery of Patriot launchers.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan takes delivery of Patriot launchers.

text.p: Taiwan on Wednesday took delivery of four launching vehicles for U.S.-made Patriot missiles, part of a drive to improve its defences in the face of rival China's army modernisation, the United Evening News reported.
The report, accompanied by a photograph of one launcher in northern Keelung port, said four of the truck-like vehicles were delivered to Taiwan early on Wednesday.
Two more launching vehicles were expected to arrive in southern Kaohsiung later in the day, it said.
There was no word as to when the Gulf War-tested Patriot anti-aircraft and anti-missile missiles themselves would be delivered.
Taiwan's defence ministry declined to comment.
The Pentagon announced in September 1993 that Taiwan planned a private purchase from U.S. defence giant Raytheon Co of a Patriot-based "Modified Air Defence System" for an estimated US$175 million.

The Pentagon said the deal was to be handled between Taipei and Raytheon, which would provide the system's firing units, missiles and related hardware, as well as logistics and spare parts support, installation assistance and training.
Taiwan's defence ministry says it decided to build a Patriot missile base in the capital Taipei to defend against missile threats from communist arch rival China.

China, which has regarded Taiwan as a rebel-held province since a civil war ended in 1949, asserts a right to use force to prevent moves by Taiwan towards independence and away from its stated advocacy of eventual reunification with the mainland.

China rattled Taiwan with war games and unarmed missile tests in nearby waters in the run-up to last year's presidential election in what Beijing achknowledged was a bid to intimidate Taiwan voters against independence.
The United States responded by sending two aircraft carrier groups to the region, a dramatic show of support for Taiwan despite having switched diplomatic ties to Beijing in 1979.
